**Merge** joins two branches, creates merge commit. History shows exactly what happened.

**Rebase** replays your commits on top of target branch. History looks linear, no merge commit.

---

## Merge

```
      A---B---C  feature
     /         \
D---E---F---G---H  main  (H = merge commit)
```

- Preserves exact history
- Merge commit shows "these branches joined here"
- Safe on shared/public branches
- Clutters log with many merge commits on busy repos

## Rebase

```
              A'--B'--C'  feature (replayed on top of G)
             /
D---E---F---G  main
```

- Rewrites commit hashes (A→A', B→B', C→C')
- Clean linear history, easy `git log`
- **Never rebase public/shared branches** — rewrites history others depend on

---

## When to use

| Situation | Use |
|-----------|-----|
| Merging finished feature to main | **Merge** (or squash merge) |
| Updating feature branch with latest main | **Rebase** (keep history clean) |
| Shared branch (main, develop) | **Merge** always |
| Solo feature branch cleanup before PR | **Rebase** |
| Need to preserve exact "what happened when" | **Merge** |

---

## Key tradeoff

**Merge** = honest history, safe, noisy.
**Rebase** = clean history, dangerous on shared branches, rewrites reality.

Golden rule: **rebase local, merge public**.
